subject: Post-demo: latency acceptance walkthrough & traffic-slicing plan for hosted migration
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Samir Shah <samir@nimblehealth.io>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Post-demo: latency acceptance walkthrough & traffic-slicing plan for hosted migration

Samir — thanks for the demo today. Quick recap and concrete asks so we keep momentum: 

What I heard / recap:
- Your core inference path currently uses your incumbent provider for both streaming and non-streaming requests.
- Typical steady-state qps: ~10 r/s (600 r/min); peak bursts up to ~20 r/s (1,200 r/min).
- Streaming is ~15-20% of calls, typical streaming window ~4–8s, avg tokens ~150–180.

Open asks (can you confirm by EOD tomorrow?):
1) Current production e2e numbers you are comfortable sharing for p95 and p99 (incumbent).
2) Typical concurrent open requests during peak minutes (we need a 95th percentile concurrency envelope).
3) Any batching or client-side multiplexing that would affect request patterns.
4) Key success criteria for considering hosted migration: target p95/p99 deltas vs incumbent and any non-latency constraints (e.g., allowed token loss, truncation policy).
5) Procurement timeline & any RFQ docs (if you can share).

Next steps we propose from Redwood:
- Shadow test (traffic-sliced) at 5–10% of production for 72 hours to capture realistic tails.
- Run the test with the same token sizes & streaming mix you provided; we’ll surface p95/p99 breakdowns per route and infra.
- Provide a short playbook: concurrency tuning, streaming window limits, KV cache notes, and rollback criteria.

If you can attach the last week’s tail snapshot (p95/p99 distributions) and any procurement doc, that’ll accelerate scheduling.

Thanks again — I’ll coordinate dates with Ben and Logan.

—
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com

From: Samir Shah <samir@nimblehealth.io>

Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 18:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo: latency acceptance walkthrough & traffic-slicing plan for hosted migration

Thanks Marissa — great session. Attaching a quick snapshot and RFQ stub. Answers inline below.

1) Incumbent production e2e averages (last 7 days): p95 = 275 ms, p99 = 1200 ms. These include network + model execution + app-side processing.
2) Peak concurrent open requests (95th percentile) = ~12 concurrent requests. During burst windows we’ve seen up to 20 concurrent.
3) No server-side batching today — all single-request RPCs from clients. No multi-request multiplexing.
4) Primary acceptance criteria: user-facing p95 <= 220 ms and p99 <= 600 ms would be ideal — if hosted can hit that we consider migration. Secondary: no increase in error rate, and streaming sessions must stay intact (no premature truncation).
5) Procurement timeline: target is ~6 weeks from signed SOW to order. RFQ attached: nimble_procurement_rfq_2026-11.pdf

Attachments: nimble_latency_snapshot_11-22.json, nimble_procurement_rfq_2026-11.pdf

—

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Samir Shah <samir@nimblehealth.io>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 09:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo: latency acceptance walkthrough & traffic-slicing plan for hosted migration

Samir — quick technical clarifications so the shadow test is scoped correctly. Copying the relevant snippet of Marissa’s note for context.

A few asks from engineering:
- Confirm typical request payload size (tokens and approximate payload bytes). You said ~150 tokens avg — can you give an average JSON payload size?
- Is there any client-side retry logic or exponential backoff we should mirror in the shadow run?
- Streaming specifics: do you use server-sent events (chunked) with keep-alive or websocket-based streaming? We need to mirror the same streaming framing to get realistic tail behavior.
- Cold-start behavior: does your incumbent have periodic model loads? Any nightly batch windows where cold starts spike?
- KV cache: are you pinning prompts or keys for reuse which would materially change cache hit ratio?

Proposal for the shadow test config (we can iterate):
- Duration: 72 hours; traffic-slice: 7% of production (steady-state + proportional bursts injected).
- Traffic shaping: preserve the streaming/non-streaming ratio; streaming sessions should be kept alive and cut after the same window you use today.
- Success criteria (for go/no-go): p95_delta <= +30 ms vs incumbent and p99_delta <= +150 ms during steady-state; we’ll also flag any >2x increase in error rates or streaming truncations. These are conservative; Marissa, we should align with Samir’s procurement/decision timeline.

If that config looks good I’ll draft the test harness and the traffic replay script.

—
Ben Carter
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com
From: Samir Shah <samir@nimblehealth.io>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@nimblehealth.io
Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 13:47:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo: latency acceptance walkthrough & traffic-slicing plan for hosted migration

Ben — answers below, thanks.

- Avg payload: ~2.4 KB JSON (headers + prompt + metadata). Avg tokens ~155 as noted.
- No client-side batching and minimal retry logic: clients do one retry after 500 ms for timeouts, exponential backoff not widely used.
- Streaming: chunked HTTP/1.1 server-sent events (SSE) with keep-alives; sessions stay open until model returns EOS or client cancels.
- Cold starts: we have scheduled model refreshes and occasional nightly restarts; cold-start spikes typically in a 20–40 minute window after the nightly job.
- KV cache: negligible — we don’t pin prompts at the provider level.

We’re okay with a 7–10% shadow slice for the test and Dec target dates look feasible. Procurement team looped on schedule and RFQ.

—
Samir
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Samir Shah <samir@nimblehealth.io>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>, procurement@nimblehealth.io
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 10:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo: latency acceptance walkthrough & traffic-slicing plan for hosted migration

Thanks Samir — this is perfect. Confirming next steps and dates so procurement can align: 

1) Redwood will run a 72-hour shadow test with a 7% traffic slice starting 2026-12-07 00:00 PT (ending 2026-12-10 00:00 PT).
2) Test config we’ll use (baseline): preserve 15–20% streaming mix, avg payload 2.4KB, streaming framing = SSE. We’ll mirror the retry behavior (single retry @ 500 ms).
3) Acceptance gate we’ll observe: steady-state p95 <= 230 ms and p99 <= 650 ms (these are the operational thresholds we recommend for the initial go/no-go). If we see p99 blow up during nightly restarts we’ll annotate that window separately — it won’t auto-fail the test but it is a risk signal.
4) Tech sync to walk through test harness and replay script: 2026-12-03 09:00 PT — I’ve added a calendar invite (link above).
5) Procurement: we’ll provide an SOW draft after the test; Samir, you mentioned a ~6-week procurement runway which aligns with a Jan activation if all goes well.

Deliverables from Redwood before the test: test config doc, traffic-replay artifact, expected metrics dashboard (p50/p95/p99, error rates, streaming truncations), and runbook for rollback. Ben and Logan will own execution.

Thanks — looking forward.

—
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
